test_title: PYST 59: SSC GD Constable - Quantitative Aptitude (Held on: 14th November 2021 Shift 1)
subject: maths
question: Three years ago, the ratio of the age of A to that of B was 8 ∶ 9. Five years hence, the ratio of the age of A to that of B will be 10 ∶ 11. If at present, C is 8 years younger than A, then the ratio of the present age of B to that of C is:
solution:
**Given:**

Ratio of ages of A and B (3 years ago) = 8 : 9

Ratio of ages of A and B (5 years hence) = 10 : 11

C = A - 8 (C is 8 years younger than A)

**Calculation:**

C = A - 8 ----(1)

Ratio of ages of A and B at present = 8x + 3/9x + 3 = 10x - 5/11x - 5 ----(2)

⇒ 8x + 3/9x + 3 = 10x - 5/11x - 5 

∴ By cross multiplication,

⇒ 88x² - 7x -15 = 90x² -15x -15

⇒ 2x² - 8x = 0

⇒ x(2x - 8) = 0

⇒ x = 0, x = 4 (possible value)

Putting x = 4 in equation (2) we get,

A present age = (8x + 3) = 35 years 

B present age = (9x + 3) = 39 years

From equation (1) we get,

C present age = 27 years

Ratio of present ages of B and C = 39/27 = 13 : 9

**∴ The present ratio of B and C is 13 : 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

Ratio of ages of persons remains same at any given year.
